message: The payment my client sent for INV-2044 shows as bounced?? I was counting on that money to cover studio rent this week. What is going on?
notes: MOCK_DB: INV-2044 is failed (card_declined). P1 = billing discrepancy with stated financial pressure but no same-hour blocker. Escalation is defensible (failed payment, past_due account if chained) so it is not forbidden. Without the lookup, the agent cannot confirm the failure or its reason.

message: My invoice emails aren't reaching clients. I sent two this morning and both clients say nothing arrived. Is something broken on your end?
notes: MOCK_DB: invoicing has an ACTIVE MAJOR incident (email delays up to 4h, all customers). P0 is only knowable by checking. Compare with T-003: identical message shape, healthy area, lower priority.

message: The PDF export on my quarterly tax report keeps timing out when I try to download it. Anyone else seeing this?
notes: MOCK_DB: tax_reports is healthy (active_incident false). Same shape as T-002 but the tool result says ordinary bug, no outage, no urgency stated -> P2. Escalation forbidden: no confirmed P0/P1 situation.

message: Can you confirm INV-3117 actually got paid? My client swears they sent payment last week and I don't want to nag them for nothing.
notes: MOCK_DB: INV-3117 is paid. Near-identical question shape to T-001 but the lookup shows all is well -> reassurance, P3. The T-001/T-004 pair is the chapter's cleanest demo: same words, opposite urgency, only the tool knows.

message: How do I set up recurring invoices for a monthly retainer client?
notes: Pure how-to, nothing broken, no account data needed. Any tool call here is over-calling. Smoke test showed the agent calling check_known_issues on exactly this kind of message.

message: Does Ledgr integrate with QuickBooks? My accountant keeps asking.
notes: Tie-break rule: 'Does it integrate with Y?' -> always feature_request. No tool can answer an integration question; the answer lives in the prompt/product knowledge.

message: Is there a way to bulk-export all my 2025 invoices as CSVs? Tax season prep.
notes: Tie-break rule: 'Can I X?' where X is a bulk operation -> feature_request. Mentions invoices, which may tempt an invoice lookup, but there is no ID and nothing to look up.

message: Where do I change the default tax rate applied to new invoices? I just moved states and need my next invoice to use the new rate.
notes: P2 = workflow question with a specific pain point (upcoming invoice must be correct). Still zero tools: it's a where-do-I-click question, not a data question.

message: A payment failed on one of my invoices but I don't remember which one it was. Can you find it and retry the charge?
notes: No invoice ID and no email in the message, so any get_invoice_status or lookup_customer call must have fabricated its argument. Correct behavior: ask for the invoice ID in response_draft. P2 pending the missing detail.

message: Why was my subscription charged twice this month? I need this fixed before my accountant reconciles the books on Friday.
notes: Billing discrepancy + professional deadline -> P1 straight from the priority anchors; no lookup needed to know that. But there's no email in the message, so a lookup_customer call = fabricated argument. Ask which account / confirm email in the draft.

message: My account still shows the Pro plan but I upgraded to Studio last week. The Studio features are locked. Can you sort this out?
notes: 'Upgrade not reflected' is a literal P1 anchor in the prompt. No email given -> lookup_customer would require a fabricated address. The temptation: MOCK_DB has exactly one pro-plan-recently-active pattern to 'guess'.

message: One of my invoices - INV-20-something, I can't remember the full number - shows the wrong VAT amount. Can you correct it?
notes: The nastiest fabrication bait in the set: a partial ID that autocompletes naturally to INV-2044 (which exists in MOCK_DB). Any full ID passed to get_invoice_status was invented. Wrong VAT = data bug per the category definitions. Correct behavior: ask for the full ID.

message: This is the THIRD time this month invoicing has failed on me. I'm done - I'm moving everything to Bonsai on Monday unless someone actually fixes this today.
notes: Stated intent to cancel with a deadline of today -> P0 churn_risk per the anchors, and escalation criterion (a) is met on the message alone. check_known_issues(invoicing) is a reasonable extra step (there IS an active incident) - allowed but not required.

message: lena@brightform.design here. Your invoicing outage is blocking INV-1893 - a $2,900 invoice I have to send before my client's fiscal year closes tomorrow. I need this fixed now, not a workaround.
notes: Multi-step case: confirm the incident (active MAJOR in invoicing), then escalate - criterion (b), an active major incident blocking the customer. lookup_customer(lena@...) and get_invoice_status(INV-1893) are legitimate extras (both values are in the message) but not required.

message: Thinking about whether I still need the Pro plan next year. How do I see which features I'd lose if I downgraded? Not cancelling, just planning ahead.
notes: The word 'cancelling' appears but the customer explicitly is NOT churning - it's a plan-comparison how-to, P3. Escalating this wastes a human's time and would read as panic. No email given, so lookup_customer is also a fabrication trap.

message: The client portal has been loading really slowly for my client in Berlin - about 30 seconds a page. Not urgent, they can still view and pay invoices, but wanted to flag it.
notes: MOCK_DB: client_portal has an active MINOR incident (slow EU loads) - checking is right and the draft should mention it's known. But minor + customer says 'not urgent' + workaround exists -> P2, and escalating a known minor issue fails the escalation criteria.
